briefing: The standout this week is Blackknife, a query-free black-box rewiring attack on heterogeneous GNNs whose degree-preserving edits evade common defenses. Financial crime is the busiest application area, with money-mule and account-takeover detectors showing graph models beating strong tree baselines at bank scale. On the methods side, a RelBench study finds that simple propagation baselines recover much of what heterogeneous GNNs achieve.

stories.title: Dual Graph Neural Networks for Social Bot Detection
stories.summary: Combines a social-relation graph with an auxiliary behavior-similarity graph for bot detection. Text embeddings contribute most, the behavior branch matters mainly for a small set of covered users, and threshold calibration substantially improves bot recall.
stories.whyItMatters: It’s an honest look at where the graph signal actually helps in bot detection, and how much calibration matters.
stories.researchAngle: Evaluate adaptive bots that mimic benign behavior similarity, an evasion attack aimed at the auxiliary graph.

stories.title: Money-Mule Detection as a Relational Learning Problem: A Study on the RBIH NFPC Dataset
stories.summary: Treats a bank’s relational schema directly as a heterogeneous graph and scores accounts with HeteroGraphSAGE, using strict time cutoffs so the model never sees post-flag evidence. On five years and 400 million transactions, it catches about nine in ten held-out mules at 83% precision and outperforms XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost, mainly on recall deep in the alert queue.
stories.whyItMatters: It’s a rare large-scale, leakage-controlled comparison of GNNs against strong tree baselines on real financial-crime data.
stories.researchAngle: Mule networks are adversarial: study how much a mule ring can evade the detector by reshaping its own transfers, using the Blackknife-style degree-preserving perturbations.

stories.title: Blackknife: Query-Free Black-Box Rewiring Attacks on Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks
stories.authors: Honglin Gao, Junhao Ren, Lan Zhao, Yue Yang, Peilin Du, Jindong Chang, Gaoxi Xiao
stories.summary: An evasion attack on heterogeneous GNNs that never queries the victim model. The attacker sees only the target nodes’ one-hop structure, labels and features, trains a surrogate on what it can observe, and rewires edges with swaps that keep each node’s per-relation degree unchanged. It reaches competitive success rates against five victim architectures and three defenses.
stories.whyItMatters: Strict black-box, query-free, degree-preserving perturbations are close to a realistic threat model, and they slip past defenses that look for degree anomalies.
stories.researchAngle: Test whether certified-robustness or structure-learning defenses hold up under degree-preserving rewiring, or port the attack to fraud and AML graphs, where an attacker controls only their own accounts’ edges.

stories.title: Revisiting Simple Baselines for Relational Deep Learning
stories.authors: Viet The Nguyen, Vijay Prakash Dwivedi, Gunther Gust
stories.summary: On RelBench, fixed low-pass feature propagation followed by an MLP recovers much of the performance of heterogeneous GNNs, and Correct-and-Smooth label propagation adds more. The catch is that label propagation needs a separately built meta-graph linking target entities.
stories.whyItMatters: It’s a useful sanity check on how much architectural complexity relational deep learning actually needs.
stories.researchAngle: Check whether these simple baselines are also more robust or less privacy-leaky than full heterogeneous GNNs, which would be a nice trustworthiness-versus-accuracy paper.

stories.title: JaGNet: Detection, Identification and Position Error Correction of GNSS Jamming with Deep Temporal Graphs
stories.authors: Ivana Kesić, Aljaž Blatnik, Carolina Fortuna, Blaž Bertalanič
stories.summary: A heterogeneous graph convolutional LSTM over receiver-and-satellite star graphs detects GNSS jamming from standard receiver output, identifies jammer type and power, and corrects the position only when jamming is present. It flags 99.8–99.9% of jammed windows with at most 1% false positives, versus about 65% for the receiver’s built-in monitor, and generalizes to field data.
stories.whyItMatters: GNSS jamming hits transit, fleets and vehicles, and this works from ordinary receiver output without raw pseudoranges.
stories.researchAngle: Extend it from jamming to spoofing, or evaluate it against an adaptive jammer that tries to stay under the detector’s threshold while still shifting position.

stories.title: VulLink: A Dynamic Open-Access Vulnerability Graph Database for Cybersecurity Data Mining
stories.authors: Luat Do, Jiao Yin, Jinli Cao, Hua Wang
stories.summary: A continuously updated graph database that links NVD, CVE, CWE, Exploit-DB and CVE Details entries into typed entities and relationships, with a web interface, public API, exportable subgraphs and precomputed language-model embeddings. The authors demonstrate exploitability prediction using heterogeneous graph context.
stories.whyItMatters: It’s a ready-made, live heterogeneous graph for security GNN research, which saves weeks of ETL work.
stories.researchAngle: Use it as a benchmark for temporal link prediction, such as forecasting which CVEs get exploits, with strict time-based splits to avoid leakage.

stories.title: GNNs in 2026: PyG passes 32M downloads; real-time GNN inference reaches graph databases
stories.summary: An industry overview of GNN adoption in 2026. It reports PyG passing 32 million PyPI downloads and notes that Amazon Neptune now integrates with the open-source GraphStorm library to serve GNN predictions from on-demand subgraphs in under a second.
stories.whyItMatters: Serving GNNs from live graph databases changes the threat model, since inference-time attacks no longer need training access.
stories.researchAngle: Study query-based model extraction and link stealing against GNN endpoints served from graph databases.

stories.title: Dual-Scale Relational Graph Transformers for Ecosystem-Aware Fraud Detection (HERMES)
stories.authors: Mohsen Nayebi Kerdabadi, Xinrou Li, Yao Xiao, Zijun Yao, Xin Sun
stories.summary: HERMES pairs a local relation-aware graph transformer over a time-safe session neighborhood with a global component that tracks the state of the fraud ecosystem over time. On over 130 million sessions from a large US bank, it cuts customer friction by 44% and raises fraud recall by 25% relative to the production system. It was accepted at the GDDL workshop at NeurIPS 2026.
stories.whyItMatters: It brings graph transformers to account-takeover fraud at production scale, with an explicit answer to concept drift.
stories.researchAngle: The global ‘ecosystem tokens’ could become a poisoning target: test whether coordinated fraud campaigns can shift them to lower detection for later attacks.

stories.title: Graph unlearning: Efficient node removal in graph neural networks
stories.summary: Proposes efficient node-unlearning methods for GNNs, evaluated on Cora, Citeseer and Pubmed, using membership inference attacks to check that the removed nodes’ influence is actually gone.
stories.whyItMatters: Unlearning is becoming a compliance requirement, and checking it with MIAs is the standard but weak test.
stories.researchAngle: Apply recent unlearning-inversion attacks, which exploit the before/after difference between model versions, to these methods. Passing a single-model MIA doesn’t mean passing a two-model one.
